agent_notes: יוצאת is read three ways. (a) 'going out' of captives or of the city's people into exile, with פרץ a breach in the wall (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Metzudat David); (b) 'no [animal] going out of bounds' (Meiri); (c) 'miscarriage' (BBE 'cows give birth safely'; STEPBible 'abortion', following the Aramaic/rabbinic use of יוצאת for a premature birth). I kept the literal 'going out' and say in the commentary that (c) is the reading that BBE chose and that fits the cattle context. Not settled.

אלופינו: the commentators (Rashi apart) take it as 'our oxen' (Radak, Metzudat Zion, citing Deut 7:13 שגר אלפיך). Rashi alone reads it as 'our chiefs', which is the other sense of the same root אלף (leader of a clan) and which Meiri also records from the rabbis. I translated 'oxen' and kept the double meaning in the commentary.

מסבלים: 'loaded'. Ibn Ezra and Radak: they bear loaded wagons or the work of ploughing; Meiri and Metzudat David: loaded with flesh, so fat that it is a burden. I chose 'loaded' without deciding between strength and fatness.
